a_records.quote: Theorem 2. Let X1 , . . . , Xn be independent random variables with Xi ∼ Fré(µ, θi , α), i = 1, . . . , n, and Y1 , . . . , Yn be independent random variables with Yi ∼ Fré(µ, θi∗ , α), i = 1, . . . , n. If (1/θ1 , . . . , 1/θn ) ⪰w (1/θ1∗ , . . . , 1/θn∗ ), then Xn:n ≥rh Yn:n .
a_records.family: Fréchet Fré(µ,θi,α); common µ, α; differing scales θi

hypotheses.formal: weak submajorization (subscript w: Σ_{i>=j} x(i) >= Σ y(i)); the printed '(θ1,...,θ1n)' carries superscript 1/θi = ti in the proof

a_records.ambiguity: Hypothesis is on reciprocals 1/θi (text layer shows 'θ1,...,θ1n'); uses Lemma 2's weak-submajorization implication. Generalizes Theorem 2 of Gupta et al. from ≤st to ≥rh.

b_records.quote: Theorem 2. Let X1, . . . , Xn be independent random variables with Xi ∼ Fré(µ, θi, α), i = 1, . . . , n, and Y1, . . . , Yn be independent random variables with Yi ∼ Fré(µ, θi∗, α), i = 1, . . . , n. If (1/θ1, . . . , 1/θn) ≽w (1/θ1∗, . . . , 1/θ∗n), then Xn:n ≥rh Yn:n.
b_records.family: Fréchet Fré(µ, θi, α); common location µ and shape α, heterogeneous scales θi vs θi*
b_records.compared: reciprocal scale vectors (1/θi) under weak upper majorization
